## T.S. Eliot {background-image="images/threeWiseMonkeys/640.jpg" background-opacity="0.05"}

### *Burnt Norton* (Four Quartets)

> "Neither plenitude nor vacancy. Only a flicker  
> Over the strained time-ridden faces  
> **Distracted from distraction by distraction**  
> Filled with fancies and empty of meaning  
> Tumid apathy with no concentration..."

::: notes
Relates directly to smartphone loops, notification checking, and fragmented attention (Lecture 5).
:::

---

## Leila Chatti {background-image="images/threeWiseMonkeys/640.jpg" background-opacity="0.05"}

### *All day, the world makes its demands*

::: {.r-fit-text}
All day, the world makes its demands.  
There's so much of it, world  
begging to be noticed.  
:::

::: notes
Used in Lecture 1 to introduce why selective attention is essential in a world overloaded with sensory input.
:::

---

## Mary Oliver {background-image="images/threeWiseMonkeys/640.jpg" background-opacity="0.05"}

### *Sometimes*

> "Instructions for living a life:  
> **Pay attention.**  
> **Be astonished.**  
> **Tell about it.**"

<br>

*(From *Yes! No!*)*:

> **"To pay attention, this is our endless and proper work."**

::: notes
Emphasizes top-down, deliberate focus as an active, effortful discipline.
:::

---

## W.H. Auden {background-image="images/threeWiseMonkeys/640.jpg" background-opacity="0.05"}

### *Musée des Beaux Arts*

> "About suffering they were never wrong,  
> The old Masters: how well they understood  
> Its human position...  
> In Brueghel's Icarus, for instance: how everything turns away  
> Quite leisurely from the disaster; the ploughman may  
> Have heard the splash, the forsaken cry,  
> But for him it was not an important failure..."

::: notes
Illustrates inattentional blindness and selective attention: dramatic events occurring in plain sight are missed when attentional focus is elsewhere.
:::

---

## Wisława Szymborska {background-image="images/threeWiseMonkeys/640.jpg" background-opacity="0.05"}

### *Distraction*

> Szymborska writes of physical presence coupled with mental absence—a detached state of mind like:  
>  
> *"a nail stuck only halfway in the wall."*

::: notes
Captures mind-wandering and the subjective gap between sensory registration and conscious awareness.
:::

---

## Sue Ellson {background-image="images/notificationDetoxPhoneOnly.png" background-opacity="0.1"}

### *The Great Unfocus*

> "A haze of electrons and light,  
> Distracted by the buzz and the chime,  
> Pulled away from the present sight,  
> Trading focus for a fragment of time."

::: notes
A modern reflection on bottom-up digital alerts hijacking top-down concentration.
:::
